text:
maria: quick heads up — ran a multi-GPU TP run with INT8 quant on resnet-like arch, 8 GPUs. We see ~18% drop in tokens/sec vs baseline fp16. all-reduce time jumped, and KV cache hit pattern looks off. attaching quick stats below.
cheng: can you paste the perf trace? nvprof/nvtx or our perf-agent timeline would help.
maria: throwing some numbers: compute kernel steady ~42ms per microbatch, all-reduce went from 11ms -> 27ms (per step) after int8 compile, end-to-end tokens/sec down 18%. kv-cache flushes at step boundaries spike latency by +60ms occasionally.
sam: sounds like kernel selection changed for the matmul path — int8 lowering might be picking an algorithm that serializes or increases kernel launches. did the compilation pick cublasLt or our fallback?
maria: our compile log shows: "selected GEMM kernel: int8_fallback_v2". FP16 used cublaslt_gemm_fast.
evan: that fallback is known to increase launch overhead. Also check NCCL allreduce pattern — if the int8 path reduced compute time slightly, comm becomes relatively more dominant and we lose overlap. any overlap stats?
maria: overlap looked worse — timeline shows compute and comm not overlapping: compute finishes, then a 20ms gap, then all-reduce. NVTX trace attached (snippet):
```
[timeline] step 102: compute end @ 1020.3ms
[timeline] step 102: allreduce start @ 1020.35ms (+50us)
[timeline] allreduce 27.2ms
[timeline] kv-flush 64.1ms spike at step 120
```
cheng: kv cache spike is worrying. Is each TP shard doing its own prefix eviction and writing out? That could create serialized PCIe traffic.
zara: also check our batching heuristics — smaller microbatches increase relative allreduce frequency. If int8 reduces memory, we might be splitting differently unintentionally. What was microbatch size?
maria: microbatch = 4, global batch = 32 (tp shards 8). When we switched to int8 compilation we enabled a permissive batch packer that changed slice sizes slightly — we see more small slices at tail.
sam: action item: force the batcher to use fixed slices to remove batching variance, then repro. Also force cublasLt for int8 if available, or run our tuned int8-kernel set.
evan: try these toggles locally:
```bash
export NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1
export NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=NVL
# force cublasLt path (runtime flag)
REDCONF_FORCE_CUBLASLT_INT8=1 ./run_tp.sh --compile
```
maria: will try. also noticed FP8 scaling issue in a separate run: dynamic scale factor sometimes spikes causing quant overflow and NaNs in gelu outputs. fp8 run had correct throughput but quality regressions.
cheng: FP8 scale blowups are usually due to per-layer max not clamped. Add a clamp to scale update and retry. we also have local heuristics: if scale > 1e4 then fallback to fp16 for that op.
zara: for kv-cache: propose centralizing cache flushes so they happen in a coordinated epoch across TP ranks to avoid PCIe storms. Even a simple staggered flush offset by rank*2ms would help.
sam: agree. For comm/compute overlap: enable NCCL async progress (if not already) and consider using CUDA graphs for the steady-state to reduce kernel launch noise.
maria: repro plan: 1) fixed-slice batcher 2) force cublasLt int8 3) clamp fp8 scales 4) stagger kv flush. I'll run an isolated 8-GPU job and post traces.
evan: if you can, collect per-kernel launch counts too — high numbers indicate fragmentation. Also ping infra to check PCIe link utilization during the job.
perf-bot: perf-dashboard: https://perf.redwood.internal/dashboards/tp-int8-kv?run=1841234567 — auto-collected traces uploaded.
maria: thanks — will iterate and post back. if I don't get deterministic repro, I'll bisect the compiler flag that picked int8_fallback_v2.
cheng: will open a follow-up issue: RED-TP-INT8-1841 with logs and action items. assigning to maria + sam. :thumbsup:
